transcript:
[00:00] Alex Moreno: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we can start. Uh, quick roll call?
[00:06] Maya Torres: Maya here.
[00:08] Ethan Rios: Ethan here.
[00:10] Claire Dunn: Claire on.
[00:12] Priya Shah: Priya from Redwood.
[00:14] Daniel Kim: Daniel, CSM.
[00:16] Alex Moreno: Cool. Agenda — go over last week's lab numbers, anomalies at the tail, and next steps. Priya, do you want to kick off with the runbook results?
[00:28] Priya Shah: Yeah. So we re-ran the canonical harness with Horizon's sample traces — about 60 RPS ish steady, 8k token tail cases included. Quick headline: median was ok, about 80 to 120 ms per token, P95 for our served model was ~180ms token-latency equivalent, while the baseline IncumbentAI runs that Horizon provided were averaging P95 ~420ms in the same config.
[00:52] Ethan Rios: Wait, that delta is pretty big. Are these apples-to-apples? Sequence length distribution, cuda devices?
[00:59] Priya Shah: Good question. We matched model size, sequence truncation at 8k, and used comparable vCPU/gpu slots in the lab — approximate A100-80 slice equivalent. But there are a few differences: Redwood enabled continuous batching + async KV cache warmup; baseline run didn't have prefix caching on. Also we used an int8 quant profile on the model for the pilot run.
[01:20] Maya Torres: The inc- provider said they had lower p50 but some p99 spikes due to garbage collection and heap thrash. We saw some occasional spikes too in your dashboard earlier this week — why would Redwood show more consistent tail?
[01:32] Priya Shah: Two things — request routing and batching heuristics: we have an adaptive batch ceiling that drops batch size when queue wait hits the latency SLO. The other is our prefix/KV cache which avoids re-computation for long conversation prefix tokens. But I wanna be transparent — when the cache isn't primed for a cold conversation we did see larger p99 spikes; that was in the 800–1200ms token latency for some cold flows.
[01:56] Alex Moreno: To be clear, baseline numbers you provided did not have prefix caching, right?
[02:01] Ethan Rios: Correct, they said they didn't have the same prefix behavior; they rely on larger GPU instances to absorb variance.
[02:07] Priya Shah: Right so when we're warm we win on tail. When cold we can see spikes. We experimented with a short rewarm window and prefetch heuristics that dropped cold p99 by about 350ms in our lab test.
[02:21] Claire Dunn: How about throughput? If we push concurrency up, where do we expect saturation compared to baseline?
[02:27] Priya Shah: In our throughput stress we hit linear scaling up to the config for a single shard: about 12k tokens/s aggregate with batching enabled; compared to baseline they started to queue earlier due to their single-request-per-GPU strategy. In practical terms for Horizon's traffic shape we estimate 2.3x throughput improvement per GPU.
[02:46] Maya Torres: Is that including the int8 quantization? I worry about regressions in quality.
[02:50] Priya Shah: The int8 profile we used was a mixed int8-fp16 path — we ran a small eval suite (the prompts you shared) and saw negligible delta in ROUGE/BLEU style metrics and human spot-checks in the 1–2% range. We can share the eval deck.
[03:05] Ethan Rios: Where do those quality checks live? I want to show our NLP folks.
[03:08] Priya Shah: Linked in the sheet — /shared/horizon-poc/horizon-evals-20251222.pdf. We'll also attach the raw output samples.
[03:16] Alex Moreno: You mentioned cache warmup. What's the recommended TTL and rewarm strategy for Horizon's conversational flows?
[03:21] Priya Shah: For conversational flows with high prefix reuse, TTL of 10 minutes is reasonable plus a rewarm policy that prefetches the last K tokens if a user gets active again within 60s. We have a prefetch queue that runs async for sessions with high reuse. That knocked the cold p99 down substantially in our lab.
[03:41] Maya Torres: Ok, but in production we have so many ephemeral sessions — would prefetching blow up cost?
[03:45] Priya Shah: There's a tradeoff. Our Optimize suggestions include hitting a batching sweet spot and enabling selective prefetch only for authenticated or flagged sessions. For ephemeral anonymous sessions we recommend a shorter TTL. We'll provide cost delta numbers for those policies.
[03:58] Claire Dunn: Security question: we need to confirm KMS integration and audit log retention. Is that covered in the private deployment or dedicated?
[04:05] Alex Moreno: Both Dedicated and Private options can integrate with customer KMS and forward audit logs. We'll attach SOC2 artifact and the KMS integration guide.
[04:12] Daniel Kim: Noted — Claire, we'll drop those in the shared folder after the call.
[04:18] Ethan Rios: Back to benchmarking: your sheet shows a couple of outliers at 35 and 42 minutes in the run where p99 jumps. What caused those?
[04:24] Priya Shah: Looking at logs, those align with batch build contention from a small burst where a downstream microservice delayed sending the request body. The queue saw a 120ms jitter that triggered a full batch rebuild, which spiked a handful of requests. We've added a guard to avoid rebuilding large batches if the delay is transient.
[04:41] Maya Torres: So that is more of a harness artifact?
[04:43] Priya Shah: Partially harness and partially network jitter. In production we recommend a soft timeout at the batching layer to let a late call go to a smaller fallback batch to avoid large rebuilds.
[04:55] Claire Dunn: Can Redwood do a canary routing where cold sessions get routed to baseline provider temporarily until cache warms?
[05:02] Priya Shah: Yes — we have routing policies that can route by session TTL or observed cache-hit ratio. Canary offload is supported; we can configure that as a policy.
[05:10] Alex Moreno: Let's capture a short decision: Horizon asked for a fallback policy. Priya, can you prototype a routing policy sample by Tuesday?
[05:16] Priya Shah: Yep, will do.
[05:18] Maya Torres: Also pricing. If we move to dedicated, what's the delta? You mentioned 4x A100 equiv earlier.
[05:23] Alex Moreno: I'll send a line-item estimate — includes reserved burst, monitoring retention, and a fallback buffer. We expect the TCO to be competitive given the throughput gains; I'll include per-1M token delta.
[05:34] Ethan Rios: On instrumentation — what traces do you need to reproduce our spikes?
[05:38] Priya Shah: Ideally request/response timing at token-block granularity, queue wait times, batch size per response, and model kernel timings. If you can share two representative traces (a cold and a warm one) that'd be perfect.
[05:52] Maya Torres: We'll extract those and drop them in /shared/horizon-poc/traces/.
[05:56] Claire Dunn: A couple more quick items: SLA expectations on p99 and scheduled maintenance windows.
[06:01] Alex Moreno: Dedicated comes with SLA on uptime and latency SLOs; we'll propose a p99 target in the pilot SLA and a plan for scheduled maintenance windows — default is rolling maintenance with negotiated blackout windows.
[06:12] Priya Shah: Back to the numbers: I'd like to walk through a specific sample from your sheet if that's ok — the 2025-12-22-run-7 which had the worst tail.
[06:20] Ethan Rios: Yep that's the one.
[06:22] Priya Shah: (scrolling) In that run we saw a queue backlog spike at minute 37, batch size jumped from 8 to 24 because the scheduler preferred throughput at that moment; that pushed a few requests into a longer path. We've adjusted the scheduler to cap dynamic batches at 16 for your profile which smooths tail.
[06:40] Maya Torres: If we cap at 16 does that reduce throughput materially?
[06:43] Priya Shah: Minimal impact — we lose maybe 6–8% peak throughput but P99 improves by ~28% in our lab. For Horizon's error/tolerance profile I'd recommend improving tail at the small cost.
[06:56] Claire Dunn: Who owns the change in pilot? Will it be Redwood or Horizon?
[06:59] Alex Moreno: Redwood will push the scheduler patch in the pilot lab, then we'll coordinate a canary to Horizon environment. Horizon will sign-off after internal QA.
[07:09] Ethan Rios: Ok. Regarding evals, can you produce a diff view that maps specific prompt families to regression artifacts?
[07:14] Priya Shah: Yes — we'll produce a per-prompt regression table and include raw tokens side-by-side.
[07:19] Maya Torres: Any concerns about model warmup costs?
[07:22] Priya Shah: Warmup has a cost but it's amortized if sessions re-use prefixes. For very ephemeral flows it's less efficient; we'll show three policy tradeoffs in the cost appendix.
[07:33] Claire Dunn: Let's talk about timeline — if we want to decide on January procurement, what do we need to deliver in the next two weeks?
[07:40] Alex Moreno: Priorities: 1) Priya to deliver p95/p99 matrix and raw logs; 2) Redwood to deliver pricing and Dedicated config; 3) Horizon to provide production sample traces. If those land we can plan an architecture review and procurement packet in early Jan.
[07:57] Ethan Rios: Makes sense.
[07:59] Maya Torres: A question about billing: are we billed on tokens or tokens+compute for Dedicated?
[08:04] Alex Moreno: Dedicated is reserved capacity plus usage for overage; hosted is token-based. We'll put the exact breakdown in the quote.
[08:10] Priya Shah: Small gotcha to watch for — if you enable KV persistent caching across nodes in Private mode there's a small storage footprint and delta in monthly fee; we’ll enumerate that.
[08:21] Claire Dunn: Good. Any other blockers?
[08:24] Ethan Rios: Not from platform side.
[08:25] Maya Torres: None here.
[08:27] Alex Moreno: Alright let's go to a quick live demo of the dashboard numbers — Priya?
[08:30] Priya Shah: Sharing screen now — (brief pause) ok, so this view shows per-route token latency distribution; you can see run 12 vs run 7. See the right side panel for cache hit ratio. Run 7 had a 34% cold-hit which lines up with the spikes.
[09:00] Ethan Rios: Can you filter by session id?
[09:02] Priya Shah: Yep — filtering... here's a cold session timeline. Notice the queue wait jumped before the model call.
[09:12] Claire Dunn: That queue wait — is that caused by upstream service retrying or aggregation?
[09:15] Priya Shah: Upstream aggregation. We recommend smoothing upstream dispatch.
[09:18] Maya Torres: We'll take that to infra.
[09:20] Alex Moreno: We're about 20 minutes in — want to open for any technical deep-dive requests?
[09:25] Ethan Rios: I want to see kernel runtime breakdown — how much is attention vs matmul.
[09:30] Priya Shah: Our kernel telemetry shows attention kernels dominated at smaller batch sizes, whereas matmul dominates at larger batch sizes. We'll export the kernel timing CSV for run 22.
[09:40] Maya Torres: And does Redwood do any kernel fusion that the incumbent lacks?
[09:43] Priya Shah: We do fused attention paths for long sequences which helps the 8k tests. That's a key reason we see the tail advantage.
[09:49] Claire Dunn: Any compliance risks with kernel-level telemetry?
[09:52] Alex Moreno: No customer PII leaves the node in the telemetry; logs are hashed and we support KMS encryption at rest.
[09:59] Ethan Rios: Great. A tangent: procurement wanted to know if we can get a short performance SLA clause for the pilot.
[10:04] Daniel Kim: We can draft a pilot SLA that includes baseline p95 targets and a remediation plan if not met.
[10:09] Maya Torres: Please do.
[10:11] Alex Moreno: Ok, last 10 minutes — let's confirm owners and dates. Priya — p95/p99 matrix and raw logs by 12/30. Alex — pricing and dedicated config by 12/26. Ethan — sample traces by 12/29. We'll target a caching deep-dive Jan 5. Anything else?
[10:30] Maya Torres: Can you include cost tradeoffs for prefetch TTLs?
[10:33] Priya Shah: Yes — we'll include cost appendix with three policies.
[10:36] Claire Dunn: And the procurement SLA draft.
[10:38] Alex Moreno: Yep.
[10:39] Maya Torres: Thanks everyone — useful session.
[10:41] Ethan Rios: Thanks.
[10:42] Priya Shah: Thanks, bye.
[51:30] (meeting ended)
